answer: The dawn of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Every claim climbs the basalt of verified tasks, and a reviewer at the glacier re-runs the work instead of trusting the label. The design leans on bond keyed to a hardware root, forfeited on duplicate submission, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Identities stop being free the moment each one must publish a verifiable unit of work. Written in a plain and slightly dry register, it stays short.
